methods.title: Dotted Rhythmic Pairs
methods.summary: Reverse long-short and short-long rhythms within four note pairs.
instructionSentences: This exercise develops even finger control by changing which note in each pair lasts longer.
Play dotted-eighth and sixteenth pairs, then reverse them while keeping a steady beat.

methods.title: Four Fast Notes and Four Slow Notes
methods.summary: Alternate groups of four sixteenth notes and four eighth notes.
instructionSentences: This exercise develops smooth transitions between groups of four fast and four slow notes.
Follow the printed rhythm with a steady pulse, keeping the fast groups even and relaxed.
methods.directionAboveExercise: Keep a steady pulse when changing between fast and slow notes. Play the fast group evenly and without tension.

methods.title: Two Fast Notes and Two Slow Notes
methods.summary: Alternate two-note fast and slow groups, then reverse them.
instructionSentences: This exercise develops control when switching between short groups of fast and slow notes.
Alternate two fast and two slow notes, then reverse the pattern in the second measure without changing the pulse.
methods.directionAboveExercise: Change smoothly between the fast and slow pairs without interrupting the pulse.

methods.title: One Long Note and Three Short Notes
methods.summary: Place the long note first and then last in each four-note group.
instructionSentences: This exercise develops even short notes and preparation during the longer note at each group edge.
Keep the three short notes even and use the long note to prepare your next movement without tightening.
methods.directionAboveExercise: Keep the three short notes even. Use the long note to prepare the next movement without tightening the hand.

methods.title: Moving the Long Note Within the Group
methods.summary: Move the long note through the two inner positions of each four-note group.
instructionSentences: This exercise develops a steady pulse when the longer note moves within a group.
Follow the changing long-note position without adding an accent just because a note lasts longer.
methods.directionAboveExercise: Maintain the pulse as the long note changes position. Do not add an accent simply because a note is longer.

methods.title: Long Notes Outside and Inside the Group
methods.summary: Contrast longer notes at the edges with longer notes in the middle.
instructionSentences: This exercise develops rhythmic control as longer notes move from the edges to the middle of each group.
Place longer notes at group edges in measure one and in the middle in measure two, keeping the pulse steady.

methods.title: Four-Note Groups with Rests
methods.instructions: If the selected measure contains at least four consecutive notes, divide the passage into groups of four notes. Generate an exercise in which each group is played separately, followed by a short rest. Preserve the original pitches, note order, and fingering when available.
methods.howToPractice: Play each group slowly and correctly, then gradually increase the speed.

methods.title: Gradually Expanding Note Groups
methods.instructions: If the selected measure contains at least six consecutive notes, generate an exercise that gradually adds more notes. Start with the first four notes, then add two more notes in each repetition until the entire selected passage is included. Separate the groups with rests.
methods.howToPractice: Begin with a small group of notes and gradually make it longer. Focus on playing each group correctly before adding more notes.

methods.title: Four-Note Accent Shifts
methods.instructions: If the selected measure contains at least four consecutive notes, generate two versions of the passage. In the first version, accent every fourth note, starting with the first note. In the second version, accent every fourth note, starting with the second note. Preserve the original pitches, rhythms, and note order.
methods.howToPractice: Practice slowly and focus on the accented notes while keeping the remaining notes even.

methods.title: Blocked and Broken Chords
methods.instructions: If the selected measure contains broken chords or arpeggios, identify groups of notes belonging to the same chord. In the first version, combine the notes of each group into a chord, but only if the notes can be played comfortably together. In the second version, write the same notes separately in their original order. Do not add any pitches that are not present in the original passage. Avoid chords that require uncomfortable stretching. If the harmony cannot be identified reliably, do not generate this exercise.
methods.howToPractice: Practice the chord positions slowly, then play the notes separately while keeping the hand relaxed.

methods.title: Legato and Staccato
methods.instructions: If the selected measure contains consecutive notes, generate two versions of the passage. In the first version, write the passage with legato articulation. In the second version, write the same passage with staccato articulation. Preserve the original pitches, rhythms, note order, and fingering when available.
methods.howToPractice: Practice both versions slowly, keeping the notes even and the hand relaxed.

methods.title: Hands Separately
methods.instructions: If the selected measure contains notes in both hands, generate two versions. In the first version, include only the right-hand part. In the second version, include only the left-hand part. Preserve the original pitches, rhythms, and fingering when available.
methods.howToPractice: Practice each hand separately until the passage becomes comfortable, then return to playing both hands together.
